newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russia energy ministry works on lower taxes - agency.
newsitem.headline: Russia energy ministry works on lower taxes - agency.

text.p: Russia's Fuel and Energy Ministry is working on a proposal to decrease the tax burden on companies in the energy sector, Fuel and Energy Minister Boris Nemtsov told Interfax news agency on Tuesday.
He said this was an important step towards ending the crisis in the energy complex.
"According to him, the lowering of the companies' tax burden is one of the most important conditions for bringing this branch out of crisis," Interfax said.
Nemtsov, who is also a first deputy prime minister, was quoted as saying that another major problem faced by the energy sector was its failure to attract sufficient foreign investment.
To speed up the process, Russia should introduce production sharing legislation needed to allow more foreign companies to participate in Russia's ailing oil sector, he said.
Russian and foreign oil companies producing and exporting oil in Russia have often complained that transport tariffs and taxes on production are too high.
They are also frustrated at conservative and nationalist opposition to foreign participation in Russia's oil industry among deputies in the State Duma lower house of parliament.
The Duma has blocked a list of 25 or so reserves eligible for exploitation under production sharing agreements, and has failed to pass enabling legislation also needed before the deals can proceed.
Russia produced 293 million tonnes of crude oil in 1996 (5.9 million barrels per day), down two percent from 1995 levels and the lowest total for nearly three decades.
